helpers.name: reserve_function

parameters.name: file_id
parameters.description: File ID where function will be defined

parameters.name: skip_id_naming
parameters.description: If true, skip ID embedding in name (for MCP tools, private functions excluded). Sets id_in_name=0 in database.

helpers.purpose: Reserve a function ID before writing code. Include purpose, parameters, and returns — null fields make functions invisible to future sessions.
return_statements: Use returned ID for function naming: {name}_id_{id}

MANDATORY: Include purpose, parameters, and returns fields NOW. These are the AI's primary lookup mechanism across sessions. Null fields make functions invisible to future discovery — the DB becomes just a filename index. If unsure of the signature, plan the function first, then reserve. Example: purpose='Build coin selection entry from raw data', parameters='coin: CoinEntry', returns='CoinSelectionEntry'
Ensure the parent file (file_id) has been reserved via reserve_file. Files and functions must both be tracked.
After finalization, ensure interactions are added where needed. See directive project_update_db (Branch 6: update_interactions_table) for interaction tracking workflow.
Next: write function code with ID in name → finalize_function(function_id, name, file_id)

used_by_directives.description: Reserve function ID before writing code - AI embeds ID in function name for instant lookups (function_name_id_99)
Reserve function IDs before generating function code - enables rename-proof references

implementation_notes: Returns {success: true, id: reserved_id, is_reserved: true, id_in_name: !skip_id_naming}
SQL: INSERT INTO functions (name, file_id, purpose, parameters, returns, is_reserved, id_in_name) VALUES (?, ?, ?, ?, ?, 1, ?) RETURNING id
Function name pattern: {name}_id_{id} (e.g., calculate_sum_id_42) unless skip_id_naming=true
If skip_id_naming=true: id_in_name=0, name stays as-is (for MCP tools that need clean names)

helpers.name: reserve_functions

parameters.name: functions
parameters.description: Array of function objects [{name, file_id, purpose, parameters, returns, skip_id_naming?}, ...]

helpers.purpose: Batch-reserve function IDs before writing multiple functions. Include purpose/parameters/returns for every function.
return_statements: Use returned IDs for function naming: {name}_id_{id}

MANDATORY: Include purpose, parameters, and returns fields for EVERY function. These are the AI's primary lookup mechanism across sessions. Null fields make functions invisible to future discovery — the DB becomes just a filename index. If unsure of signatures, plan functions first, then reserve.
Ensure all parent files (file_ids) have been reserved via reserve_file/reserve_files. Files and functions must both be tracked.
After finalization, ensure interactions are added where needed. See directive project_update_db (Branch 6: update_interactions_table) for interaction tracking workflow.
Next: write function code with IDs in names → finalize_functions([{function_id, name, file_id}, ...])
implementation_notes: Returns {success: true, ids: [id1, id2, ...]} in same order as input functions array
SQL: Multiple INSERT INTO functions (name, file_id, purpose, parameters, returns, is_reserved, id_in_name) VALUES (?, ?, ?, ?, ?, 1, ?) (in transaction)
IDs correspond to functions array indices: functions[0] gets ids[0], functions[1] gets ids[1], etc.
Each item has its own skip_id_naming flag - allows mixed batch with some functions having IDs, some not
id_in_name is set to !skip_id_naming for each function individually

helpers.name: finalize_function

parameters.name: skip_id_naming
parameters.description: If true, skip _id_XX pattern validation (for functions where ID naming was skipped during reservation)

helpers.purpose: Mark a reserved function as tracked after writing it. Triggers interaction and type-function relationship checks.
return_statements: WARNING: Verify purpose, parameters, and returns are populated. Functions with null fields are incomplete tracking entries — future AI sessions cannot look them up by signature. If any field is null, populate it NOW via update_function(). This is your last chance before the function is considered 'tracked'.
Verify parent file has been finalized via finalize_file. Both file and function must be finalized for complete tracking.

BLOCKED: Do NOT proceed to next task or mark work complete until interactions are added for this function. If this function calls, chains, borrows from, composes with, or pipes to ANY other tracked function, those interactions MUST be recorded via add_interaction or add_interactions. A finalized function that imports from other tracked files with zero recorded interactions = incomplete tracking. Interactions are how the AI understands the dependency graph — without them, refactoring impact analysis is blind.

TYPES_FUNCTIONS CHECK: Scan this function's parameters and returns for tracked type names. If it consumes or produces a tracked type, add the relationship via add_types_functions. Auto-infer role: returns type only → 'factory'; params AND returns same type → 'transformer'; params with boolean/Result return → 'validator'; params only → 'accessor'. This is how the AI answers 'what functions use TypeX?' without scanning all files.
If called during project_reserve_finalize: follow project_update_db directive to sync function dependencies.

used_by_directives.description: Finalize function after code written - sets is_reserved=false and updates file timestamp
Finalize function reservations after successful code generation
Finalize function reservations when updating database with new function metadata

implementation_notes: Returns {success: true, function_id: function_id, file_id: file_id}
Sets is_reserved=0, automatically calls update_file_timestamp(file_id)
SQL: UPDATE functions SET is_reserved=0, name=?, purpose=?, parameters=?, returns=? WHERE id=?
Name validation: must contain '_id_{function_id}' pattern UNLESS skip_id_naming=true
If skip_id_naming=true: skip _id_XX validation, function was reserved with id_in_name=0

helpers.name: finalize_functions

parameters.name: functions
parameters.description: Array of function objects [{function_id, name, file_id, purpose, parameters, returns, skip_id_naming?}, ...]

helpers.purpose: Batch-finalize multiple reserved functions after writing them. Triggers interaction and type-function checks for all.
return_statements: WARNING: Verify purpose, parameters, and returns are populated for ALL functions. Functions with null fields are incomplete tracking entries — future AI sessions cannot look them up by signature. If any field is null, populate it NOW via update_function(). This is your last chance before functions are considered 'tracked'.
Verify all parent files have been finalized via finalize_file/finalize_files. Both files and functions must be finalized for complete tracking.

BLOCKED: Do NOT proceed to next task or mark work complete until interactions are added for ALL finalized functions. For EVERY function that calls, chains, borrows from, composes with, or pipes to ANY other tracked function, those interactions MUST be recorded via add_interaction or add_interactions (batch). Finalized functions that import from other tracked files with zero recorded interactions = incomplete tracking. Do NOT batch-finalize functions and move on without interaction planning — the finalize → interact flow is atomic.

TYPES_FUNCTIONS CHECK: Scan ALL finalized functions' parameters and returns for tracked type names. For each function that consumes or produces a tracked type, add the relationship via add_types_functions. Auto-infer roles: returns type only → 'factory'; params AND returns same type → 'transformer'; params with boolean/Result return → 'validator'; params only → 'accessor'. This covers 80%+ of cases automatically — correct or add remaining roles manually.
If called during project_reserve_finalize: follow project_update_db directive to sync function dependencies.
implementation_notes: Returns {success: true, finalized_ids: [...]} confirming which IDs were finalized
Calls update_file_timestamp() once per unique file_id (not once per function)
SQL: Multiple UPDATE functions SET is_reserved=0 WHERE id=? (in transaction)
All operations succeed or all fail - no partial finalization
Each item has its own skip_id_naming flag - validation is per-item, not global
If skip_id_naming=true for an item, skip _id_XX pattern validation for that specific function

helpers.name: search_functions

parameters.name: search_string
parameters.description: Free-text search over function name and purpose, one or more words (e.g. 'disk space free')

parameters.name: include_details
parameters.description: If false, omit purpose/parameters/returns for lightweight listing

parameters.name: details_only
parameters.description: If true, return only id/name + purpose/parameters/returns

helpers.purpose: Search tracked functions by name or purpose with relevance ranking. Multi-word input is split into words; a row matches if ANY word prefix-matches ("disk space free" finds get_free_disk_space). Rows matching more words rank first. Punctuation is ignored, so no FTS syntax is needed or honored.
helpers.error_handling: Returns empty list when nothing matches or input has no word characters. Falls back to per-word LIKE if the FTS5 table is missing
implementation_notes: Terms built by helpers/shared/fts_query.py: tokenize_search_terms -> build_fts_match_expression ('"disk"* OR "space"*')
Ranked by bm25(functions_fts, 5.0, 1.0) — name matches weigh more than purpose matches
Fallback: build_like_clause per term when functions_fts is missing (pre-migration databases)
